n: A burst of joy: “Arise, shine!” Zion is like a woman lying in darkness who is told to stand up, because the Lord’s glory has risen on her like the sunrise. Latter-day revelation echoes this call to the Church.

f.w: Arise, shine; for thy light is come
the glory of the LORD

n: Thick darkness covers the earth and its peoples, but the Lord rises on Zion and His glory is seen on her. The contrast makes her light visible to all.

f.w: gross darkness
the darkness shall cover the earth

n: Gentile nations and kings will be drawn to Zion’s light. The gospel spreading to all nations is part of this fulfillment.

f.w: the Gentiles shall come to thy light

n: Look around! Your sons and daughters are coming home from far away, carried like children on the hip. A picture of the great gathering of Israel.

f.w: thy sons shall come from far
nursed at thy side
f.g: Carried on the hip, as mothers carried young children.

n: Zion will glow with joy and her heart will swell with wonder as the wealth of the seas and the nations streams to her.

f.w: flow together
forces of the Gentiles
f.g: The wealth or riches of the nations.

n: Caravans of camels from Midian, Ephah, and Sheba will bring gold and incense and proclaim the Lord’s praise. Christians have long seen a foreshadowing in the wise men’s gifts to the Christ child.

f.w: they shall bring gold and incense
dromedaries
f.g: Young camels used for swift travel.

f.w: Sheba
f.g: A wealthy kingdom in southern Arabia (modern Yemen), famous for incense.

n: Flocks from Kedar and rams from Nebaioth—Arabian tribes descended from Ishmael—will be accepted on God’s altar as He glorifies His temple. Ishmael’s descendants join in worship.

f.w: Kedar
Nebaioth
f.g: Ishmael’s firstborn son and the tribe from him (Genesis 25:13).

f.w: the house of my glory

n: Who are these flying like clouds, like doves to their dovecotes? Ships with white sails hurrying God’s people home—or, as some Latter-day Saints have suggested, modern travel by air.

f.w: as the doves to their windows
f.g: Like doves returning to the openings of their nesting houses.

n: Distant coastlands wait for the Lord, with the ships of Tarshish leading the way, bringing Zion’s children home along with their silver and gold, to honor the Lord.

f.w: the ships of Tarshish
f.g: Large ocean-going merchant ships; Tarshish was a distant port, perhaps in Spain.

f.w: Surely the isles shall wait for me

n: Foreigners will rebuild Zion’s walls and their kings will serve her. God struck her in anger, but now shows favor and mercy.

f.w: the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls
in my favour have I had mercy on thee

n: Zion’s gates will stay open day and night, with no fear of attack, so the wealth of nations and their kings can enter. John sees this in the New Jerusalem.

f.w: thy gates shall be open continually

n: Nations that refuse to serve Zion will perish—meaning those that fight against God’s kingdom will not last.

f.w: shall perish

n: Lebanon’s finest trees will come to beautify God’s sanctuary, the place where His feet rest. Solomon’s temple was built with Lebanon’s cedar.

f.w: The glory of Lebanon
the place of my feet

n: Children of Zion’s oppressors will bow before her and call her “The City of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” Former enemies come to honor her.

f.w: The city of the LORD

n: Once abandoned and hated, with no one passing through, Zion will become majestic forever, a joy to all generations.

f.w: eternal excellency

n: Zion will be nourished by nations and kings like a baby at the breast, and will know that the Lord is her Savior, Redeemer, and Mighty One of Jacob.

f.w: suck the milk of the Gentiles
I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer

n: Everything will be upgraded: gold instead of bronze, silver instead of iron. Her rulers will be peace and her overseers righteousness—a government of goodness.

f.w: thine exactors righteousness
f.g: Exactors = taskmasters or tax collectors; they will be replaced by righteousness.

n: No more violence, ruin, or destruction. Zion’s walls will be called Salvation and her gates Praise.

f.w: thou shalt call thy walls Salvation

n: The sun and moon won’t be needed, because the Lord Himself will be Zion’s everlasting light and glory. John uses this image for the celestial city.

f.w: the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light

n: Her sun will never set or her moon wane; the Lord will be her endless light, and her days of mourning will be over.

f.w: the days of thy mourning shall be ended

n: All her people will be righteous and inherit the land forever—a shoot God planted, the work of His hands, to show His glory.

f.w: they shall inherit the land for ever
the branch of my planting

n: The smallest will become a thousand, the weakest a mighty nation. “I the Lord will hasten it in its time.” Latter-day Saints have often applied this to the growth of the Church and the gathering.

f.w: A little one shall become a thousand
I the LORD will hasten it in his time
